Origin & botanical facts
Garlic is native to central Asia, where it
has been cultivated for more than 5,000
years.  Garlic was known to the Egyptians
as early as 3200 B.C.  When taking solemn
oaths, the ancient Egyptians swore on
garlic in much the same way people swear
on the Bible today.  Today, garlic is among
the leading vegetable crops of the world.
Some 2.3 million metric tons are pro-
duced worldwide annually.  Some of the
leading garlic-producing countries are
China, South Korea, India, Spain, the
United States, Thailand, Egypt, Turkey,
and Brazil.
